label: XG-PON1 OLT class N2, 16 ports
notes: Figures are ITU-T G.987.2 (02/2023). Downstream 9.95328 Gbit/s, Table 9-3: the modern table splits N2 into N2a (+4.0..+8.0 dBm) and N2b (+10.5..+12.5 dBm), and this row is the N2a variant - the one a normal 31 dB ODN uses. N2b is a different part, not a looser figure on this one: it buys its extra launch with a cheaper -21.5 dBm / -3.5 dBm ONU receiver, so the pair only makes sense as a pair. N2a's ONU receiver is -28.0 dBm sensitivity and -8.0 dBm overload, which is what the XG-PON ONT row carries. Upstream 2.48832 Gbit/s, Table 9-4, class N2: OLT receiver sensitivity -29.5 dBm, minimum overload -9.0 dBm. Class N2 is 31 dB of ODN loss (Table 6-1) with an attenuation range of 16-31 dB: below 16 dB the ONU overloads and needs a pad - the verdict's pad is the smallest that clears the receiver, so check it against the class's 16 dB floor before ordering. 2.0 - (-29.5) = 31.5 dB upstream against the class's 31 dB. Split ratio 64 is G.987.1 clause 8.5's minimum requirement for XG-PON; 1:128+ is an operator option the line card has to state for itself. Fibre distance: XG-PON1 must support 20 km and the TC layer 60 km (G.987.1 clause 8.6) - reach is a loss question here, so the 31 dB class bounds the run. Wavelength: XG-PON1 transmits 1575-1580 nm downstream and 1260-1280 nm upstream; the engine budgets one wavelength and defaults to 1490 down / 1310 up, whose cable attenuation (0.22 / 0.35 dB/km) sits within 0.01-0.02 dB/km of the real windows. Class figures from the recommendation, not one measured card: replace the row with the line card actually purchased before construction.
